2.text: as southern Kamchatka. Most of these became assimilated to a considerable

3.text: degree with the Koryak, though even in Kamchatka the older generation

4.text: still speaks Chukchee. On the border-line between the Chukchee and the

5.text: Koryak I came across some camps the inhabitants of which were themselves

6.text: unable to decide to which tribe they belonged, since the tribal names of

7.text: Reindeer Chukchee and Koryak are identical and the languages very similar.

8.text: NEIGHBORING TRIBES. — In the early years of the Russian invasion —
8.note: Run-in small-cap heading, keyed ASCII caps per §2.12. Two em dashes (U+2014), spaced both sides, per keying_spec.md §2.11's run-in-heading form: "LANGUAGE. — The Chukchee language is rich…"

9.text: that is, in the first half of the seventeenth century — there lived on the

10.text: large tundra west of the Kolyma some Reindeer people whom the Cossacks

11.text: also called Chukchee, and with whom they were engaged in continual petty

12.text: warfare. Two rivers of the tundra were named after them, — the Large and

13.text: the Small Chukchee. According to the tradition of the inhabitants, the oldest

14.text: Cossack settlement on the western branch of the Lower Kolyma, the village

15.text: Pokhotsk, was destroyed by them; though the story is given in an epic way,

16.text: and some of the details call to mind the tales of the Central Eskimo of

17.text: America, and must date back to a time prior to the appearance of the Russians.

18.text: Other villages were pillaged and burned down by certain Chukchee who are

19.text: reputed to have come by sea in skin boats, though at the present time there

20.text: are no maritime villages within three hundred miles to the east off these places.

21.text: The Chukchee tradition calls this people, not Chukchee, but Čaˊačên,
21.resolved: Čaˊačên = C+U+030C, a, U+02CA, a, c+U+030C, e+U+0302, n
21.note: Ethnonym set with a raised mark between the two a's, read as word stress U+02CA per keying_spec.md §4/§5.8 ("Read every raised mark as stress (U+02CA) by default, full stop"), not apostrophe — no licensing environment (post-b/p/d/t/g/k or V_V) applies here either, and this reading gives the word its one required stress mark (§5.5, culminative). Č = C+U+030C, č/ê = c/e + U+030C/U+0302 per §2.2 (settled, corpus-attested). Zoomed at 3x, --only 21@52-98.

22.text: from the Čaˊan or Čaˊwan River (“Chaun” of the maps), whose banks were
22.resolved: Čaˊan = C+U+030C, a, U+02CA, a, n; Čaˊwan = C+U+030C, a, U+02CA, w, a, n
22.note: Same raised mark as line 21, same disposition: stress U+02CA, not apostrophe (§4/§5.8). mz/ocr text had misread the second form's mark as a slash ("Ca/wan"); raster at 3x/4x (--only 22@0-72) shows the same apostrophe-shaped stress mark as the other occurrences on this page, not a slash.

23.text: their principal territory (Fig. 1). They were, however, closely connected with

24.text: them, though the Čaˊačêt spoke a language of their own. I was shown some
24.resolved: Čaˊačêt = C+U+030C, a, U+02CA, a, c+U+030C, e+U+0302, t
24.note: Same ethnonym family as line 21 but the -t (plural) ending rather than -n; same stress disposition (§4/§5.8). Zoomed at 3x, --only 24@30-65.

25.text: very old burial-mounds on both sides of the mouth of the Kolyma, filled with

26.text: large accumulations of reindeer-antlers which had been offered to the dead.

27.text: These were said to have belonged to the Čaˊačêt; the Chukchee arguing
27.resolved: Čaˊačêt = C+U+030C, a, U+02CA, a, c+U+030C, e+U+0302, t
27.note: Same word and disposition as line 24. Zoomed at 3x, --only 27@39-76.

28.text: that they could not have belonged to their own tribe, because among the

29.text: antlers of slaughtered reindeer were some which had been shed, and they offer

30.text: to the dead only the antlers of slaughtered reindeer. Some of the piles were

31.text: so old that the antlers crumbled away under one’s fingers, and were large

32.text: enough to indicate that a long range of years had elapsed during their accu-

33.text: mulation. Some of the Chukchee with whom I was acquainted even claimed

34.text: descent from a remote generation of Čaˊačên stock. The same claim was prof-
34.resolved: Čaˊačên = C+U+030C, a, U+02CA, a, c+U+030C, e+U+0302, n
34.note: Same word and disposition as line 21. Zoomed at 3x, --only 34@9-45.

35.text: fered by the Chukchee Kamakai on Cape Erri, in conversation with Wrangell.¹
35.note: Footnote 1 body reference, superscript digit per keying_spec.md §2.10, not the ASCII digit mz/ocr read as "!". Confirmed raised/small at 3x, --only 35@73-100.

36.text: The Russianized natives² along the Kolyma tell of still another extinct
36.note: Footnote 2 body reference, superscript digit (§2.10), not the ASCII digit mz/ocr read as "?". Confirmed raised/small at 4x, --only 36@14-41.

37.text: tribe, whom they call Shelags (Шелаги), and from whom is derived the name
37.note: Russian gloss in parentheses, Tier-2, keyed as printed (§1). Read at 3x (--only 37@25-55): Шелаги — ordinary modern Cyrillic, none of the pre-reform §2.7 sorts (і/ѣ/ѳ/ѵ/word-final ъ) present. mz/ocr had misread it as Latin "Hlenarn".

38.text: of Cape Shelagskoy (Cape Erri) on the Arctic. These were maritime people,

39.text: and lived somewhere along the Arctic shore. The remnants of the houses

41.text: ² The Russianized natives of the Kolyma consist chiefly of Yukaghir with a strong admixture of Russian
